In the global, connected economy, a company's supply chain and logistics are pivotal for maintaining a competitive edge.
Technological advances, new products with shorter life cycles, intense global competition, and rising customer expectations have spurred new procurement and supply chain management strategies.
Data driven decision making assists procurement and supply chain manager to design right strategies and manage performance in a competitive and dynamic business environment.
Supply chain management analytics is pivotal to data driven decision making which enables organizations to optimize processes, reduce lead times, minimize stockouts and streamline operations.

This subject focuses on the supply chain management analytics for an effective and efficient design of supply chain networks to minimize supply chain cost while managing service quality and performance.
You'll explore strategic sourcing, procurement strategies, sales and operations plan, demand-side logistics, distribution strategies, and market behaviour's impact on supply chain design.

Tactically, you'll learn cost patterns, efficient sourcing, forecasting, layout design, supply chain network optimization, data analysis, distribution, and warehousing and supply chain performance management.

These insights will help you strategise and align logistics and supply chain networks dynamically, enabling you to implement practices that enhance cost and service performance for global competitiveness.

In Financial Analytics, you will learn to utilise data to solve real-world financial challenges and drive business decisions.
Through hands-on experience with industry-standard tools and techniques, you will develop the essential skills needed in today's data-driven financial world.
You will learn to ask the right questions when approaching financial problems and identify which data can help answer them.
Central to your learning will be mastering the IMPACT analytics framework, giving you a structured approach to tackle any financial analytics project.
This framework will guide you in developing practical skills in cleaning and preparing both financial and non-financial datasets for analysis.

Throughout the subject, you will create data visualisations that tell clear stories about financial trends and patterns, while applying statistical techniques to uncover meaningful relationships in financial data.
You will build your ability to translate complex analytical findings into clear recommendations for business stakeholders, ensuring your insights drive real business value.
By the end of the subject, you will be able to approach financial problems systematically, choose appropriate analytical techniques, and communicate your insights effectively.
These skills will position you to make meaningful contributions to financial decision-making in any organisation.

This subject delves into business intelligence (BI), a comprehensive term encompassing architectures, tools, databases, analytics, applications, and methodologies aimed at facilitating interactive data access and empowering managers to make informed decisions.

It introduces decision support systems (DSS), which are computer-based systems combining models, methods, and data to tackle semi-structured or unstructured decisions, demanding user involvement and a user-friendly interface.
As high-level business decisions often fall into these categories and are data-intensive, DSS are increasingly integrated with BI techniques for enhanced problem-solving.
You'll learn about various aspects of BI and DSS, including group and intelligent support systems, web-based systems, decision optimisation, and personalised recommender systems.
Additionally, the subject teaches the design, implementation, and integration of BI techniques to bolster business decision-making processes.

This subject equips students with a rigorous understanding of portfolio analysis through quantitative tools.

This subject offers a comprehensive and rigorous exposition to the theory and practice of financial risk measurement and management.
The subject covers the value-at-risk (VaR) and expected shortfall (ES) risk measures, which are pertinent to current financial regulatory frameworks.
Parametric and non-parametric techniques, including historical and Monte Carlo simulation, to calculate or approximate risk measures are covered.
Furthermore, in view of emerging evidence of the intricate interplay of risk factors, you will also study general notions of dependence beyond linear correlation.
To more accurately model the dependence structure between risk factors, copulas are discussed in depth and applied to the calculation of risk measures.
You will then apply these risk modelling and management concepts to the analysis of market risk and operational risk, among others.

The first module will discuss the fundamental concepts of artificial neural systems and fuzzy logic theory.
It introduces the foundations of neural network learning principles including the Hebbian, Perceptron, Delta, and Widrow-Hoff learning rules.
It includes fuzzy sets, linguistic variables and approximate reasoning.
The second module covers the concept of error function 3eneralized3 using the steepest descent 3eneralized3 technique.
This will then be extended to multilayer feedforward neural networks.
Other concepts such as 3eneralized delta learning rule, feedforward recall and error back-propagation training, associative memories, matching and self-organising networks will be discussed.
Further topics will include the preliminaries and basic construction of a fuzzy controller, adaptive fuzzy logic controller, and the self-organising fuzzy logic controller.
Lastly, a basic concept of convolutional neural network and genetic algorithm are introduced.
The third module relates to advanced applications of intelligent systems.
The design and development of a semi-autonomous wheelchair using neural network classifications will be discussed.
Other advanced applications relate to the control of blood glucose in patients with diabetes using a fuzzy system.
This subject introduces you to neural networks and fuzzy theory with an engineering focus, offering hands-on experience and professional practice integration.

Through practical examples, you'll develop expertise in applying neural networks and fuzzy logic to real-world engineering applications.
